excerpt: given that generalized identity is symmetric and transitive, and that the rules R3 and R4 are truth-preserving, FACTUAL-GROUNDING entails that ground-theoretic status is preserved under factual identity. More precisely: (17) a. If p, p1, p2 … ground q and p º p* , then p*, p1, p2, … ground q. b. If p1, p2, … ground q and q º q*, then p1, p2, … ground q*.
overview: This proof-like passage shows a payoff of using identity rather than an unrelated explanatory primitive. Grounding status survives substitution by factual identity, but the result applies to a worldly conception of grounding rather than to every representation-sensitive explanatory context.
title: Grounding Identity Preservation
